title: What is a 'job', the top-level unit of work?
body: The role and authority decisions already rely on 'job' (a job's mandate, per-job context, job-scoped approvals), but the glossary doesn't define it. Proposal: a Job is one outcome you requested through Coordination, with its mandate and acceptance criteria, against at most one repository (or none, for standalone research or planning). Each job owns its handoffs, assignments, decisions and grants. Alternatives: (B) a job may span several repositories, which contradicts the v1 scope; (C) use a different name, such as 'request' or 'work item'.
rec: A, as proposed. One job targets at most one repository, and concurrent jobs are independent. A follow-up you ask for later is a new job that links to its predecessor; it does not reopen the original job.
options: C: different term (say which in notes)

title: What is the shape of the factory's durable state?
body: Hosting already decided that the daemon is the single owner of a host's factory. Options: (A) An embedded transactional database (SQLite) owned and written only by the daemon. An append-only event journal (dispatches, observations, decisions, acceptances) is written in the same transaction as the current-state records, so history is never lost and queries stay simple. (B) Mutable records only, with no journal. (C) Plain files (JSON or Markdown) in the state directory, readable and editable by hand.
rec: A. The daemon is the single writer to SQLite, with a journal plus current state, and the state directory is versioned per factory. Agents never touch the database directly. Humans inspect state through `asmai` commands and an export, not by editing files, because a hand edit can break fencing and correlation.
options: A: daemon-owned SQLite, journal + current state

title: How do agents talk to the factory: create handoffs, report results, request decisions, accept work?
body: Options: (A) `asmai` CLI subcommands that agents run from their own shell (for example `asmai handoff`, `asmai result`, `asmai decision request`, `asmai accept`). They talk to the daemon over a local Unix socket, and a per-session credential in the environment identifies the caller. (B) An MCP server that the daemon exposes to each agent. (C) Agents drop files into a mailbox directory.
rec: A. A CLI works identically in Claude and Codex, is easy to qualify and script, and matches the hook commands we already use. The CLI is a thin client, and the daemon validates everything against the caller's session identity. Each provider needs its permission allow-list configured for `asmai`. MCP stays a possible later addition, not a v1 requirement.
options: A: asmai CLI over a local socket

title: How does new work or a message reach an agent sitting in an interactive CLI?
body: Options: (A) A durable inbox plus a short nudge. The message lives in the store. When the agent is at a known input-ready boundary and automation owns input, the daemon types a one-line nudge carrying a dispatch ID, and the agent pulls the content with `asmai inbox`. The pull positively confirms delivery against that dispatch ID. (B) The daemon pastes the full message content into the terminal.
rec: A. The PTY carries only a short, correlated nudge, the content is fetched through the CLI, and the fetch serves as delivery evidence. Nudges are retried if no fetch follows, so duplicate nudges are harmless because inbox reads are idempotent by message ID. If no nudge can be delivered, for example because a human has taken input or a modal is showing, the message waits durably.
options: A: durable inbox + correlated nudge, agent pulls
B: paste full content into the PTY

title: When may a dispatch be retried automatically?
body: A dispatch is one attempt to have an agent work on something. Hosting already rules out blind retries after crashes. Options: (A) Never automatically. Any lost, stale or unknown attempt goes to the owning leader, who reconciles effects and explicitly creates a new attempt. (B) Assignments the owning leader marks as side-effect-free, such as read-only research or analysis, may be retried automatically a bounded number of times, and everything else follows A. (C) Retry automatically with backoff unless something is known to have happened.
rec: B. Side-effect-free retry is opt-in, declared per assignment by the owning leader, and bounded. Every retry is a new attempt with a new ID, so evidence from an older attempt cannot complete the new one. Anything with possible repository, git, PR or external effects goes through the leader's reconciliation.
options: B: auto-retry only declared side-effect-free assignments

title: How far does fencing reach?
body: Each leader or worker session gets a generation number from the daemon, and the daemon rejects factory-state calls such as results, acceptances and handoffs from a superseded generation. That covers factory state. External effects, such as git pushes or PR updates by a stale process, are a separate question. Options: (A) Fence factory state only. The daemon also guarantees that a superseded process is terminated before a new generation starts, and external effects are found through reconciliation. (B) Additionally route consequential external actions (push, PR create or update) through `asmai` so they are fenced too.
rec: A for v1. Because the daemon owns every process on its host, it can terminate the old process group before starting the replacement, which removes the stale-writer case. B would put AsmAI in charge of git and GitHub tooling inside every agent, a large surface for little gain on a single host.
options: A: fence factory state; terminate superseded processes first
B: also fence external actions via asmai

title: What happens to orphaned agent processes and assignments?
body: Orphans include provider processes left over from a crashed daemon, workers whose owning leader is being restored, and assignments whose job was cancelled. Options: (A) At startup the daemon terminates every agent process recorded by the previous daemon instance before starting anything, and records it. Their assignments become 'needs reconciliation'. A worker whose leader is temporarily gone keeps running, but its results queue for the leader. (B) The daemon tries to re-adopt surviving processes.
rec: A. Re-adoption isn't possible after the daemon that held the PTY has died, so terminate, record and reconcile. Results from a worker whose leader is restarting are kept and await the new leader generation's acceptance. When a job is cancelled, the owning leader stops its workers at a boundary, and work that already happened is reported, not claimed undone.
options: A: terminate leftovers, reconcile; workers outlive leader restarts
